egress.terms: The ISP product is sold per IP: the page now reads 'The fastest ISP proxy servers with unlimited sessions reserved just for you', with 'Dedicated IP Pool' and 'No Limits' (unlimited threads, not an explicit bandwidth claim). Entry is $1.80 per proxy for 24 hours, $2.70 for 30 days. The rotating residential product is from $1.75/GB; the dedicated mobile product has 'Zero bandwidth and session limits'.

interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 proxy endpoints with a dashboard API for sessions and rotation; the ISP product is a single fixed address.
tooling: any client that takes an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy: curl, rclone --http-proxy, a browser, or a WireGuard-less transparent proxy. Nothing about the debrid client needs to change except where it egresses.
chaining: One static ISP address at $2.70 per 30 days with no byte meter is the cheapest way to give a free VM a residential-class source address, which is the class a debrid service is least likely to refuse; the same vendor's metered residential pool at $1.75/GB is roughly 660 times the price at 1 TiB of monthly transfer.

limits.value: the ISP address is fixed for the billing period and shared by every process on the VM; no concurrency cap published

limits_note: The unlimited-sessions claim sits in the page description rather than in the feature list, and the feature list says 'No Limits' rather than an explicit bandwidth figure. The product is priced per IP, so a byte meter would have to be a fair-use clause, and none was read.
binding_note: At 1 TiB a month the static ISP product has no byte counter to hit and no published concurrency cap; what fails instead is the debrid side, whose terms call any proxy prohibited.

identity_cost.detail: Account and card at the dashboard; crypto is also accepted per the pricing page's payment strip. No identity document was mentioned on the pages read.

reliability_note: A single fixed address is what the debrid services' sharing detectors want to see, and it is also a single point of failure: if that IP is sold to a busy pool or gets refused, the whole stack loses its egress class at once.
confidence_note: Prices and product split are on the vendor's own pricing pages read today. Whether a debrid service accepts this address class is inferred from the class the terms name (proxy, which is prohibited) and would need one account and one download to measure.
